# OPA Architecture and Project State

Dimension covering OPA's core architecture, Rego language, data model, and project
maturity. Sources: [citations.md](../citations.md).

## Core Architecture

OPA is a general-purpose policy engine that decouples policy decision-making from
policy enforcement [4]. Applications query OPA with structured JSON input, and OPA
evaluates policies to return decisions [15]. All policy and data are kept in-memory
for low-latency evaluation [2].

OPA exposes a REST API with core endpoints [4]:
- **Data API**: POST `/v1/data/<path>` for policy decisions
- **Policy API**: manage loaded policies
- **Compile API**: POST `/v1/compile/{path}` for partial evaluation
- **Health API**: `/health?bundles=true&plugins=true`

## Rego Policy Language

Rego is a Datalog-inspired declarative language extended to support structured
document models like JSON [1]. Key characteristics:

| Feature | Details |
|---|---|
| Data types | Scalars (string, number, boolean, null), arrays, objects, sets [1] |
| Module structure | Package declaration + imports + rule definitions [1] |
| Rule types | Complete rules, partial rules (sets/objects), incremental definitions, functions [1] |
| Control flow | `if`, `not`, `every`, `else`, `with` for value substitution [1] |
| Operators | Equality (`==`), unification (`=`), assignment (`:=`), membership (`in`) [1] |
| Comprehensions | Array, object, and set comprehensions for building composite values [1] |
| Metadata | YAML annotations for title, description, authors, schemas, entrypoint [1] |

Reserved keywords include: `if`, `contains`, `some`, `in`, `every`, `not`, `with`,
`default`, `else`, `import`, `package` [1].

## Data Model

OPA operates on a unified data model where everything is a document [1]:

- **`input`**: the request data provided by the caller
- **`data`**: the base document combining loaded policies, external data, and bundles
- All documents are JSON-compatible (scalars, arrays, objects, sets)

External data can be loaded via five methods with different trade-offs [20]:

| Method | Performance | Data Size | Update Lag | Complexity |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| JWT Tokens | High | Small | Login-only | Low |
| Overload `input` | High | Small | Variable | Low |
| Bundle API | High | Medium | High (7+ min) | Medium |
| Push (Data API) | High | Medium | Low (seconds) | High |
| `http.send` | Network-dependent | Large | Zero | Medium |

## Partial Evaluation

Partial evaluation converts non-linear-time policies to linear-time policies [2].
Three optimization levels via `opa build -O`:
- **-O=0**: Disabled (default)
- **-O=1** (recommended): Partially evaluates rules not depending on unknowns
- **-O=2** (aggressive): Inlines virtual documents and applies copy propagation

Use case: generating database conditions (SQL WHERE clauses) for policy-based
filtering [4].

## CNCF Status and Project Health

| Milestone | Date |
|---|---|
| CNCF Sandbox | April 2018 [8] |
| Incubation | April 2019 [8] |
| Graduation | February 4, 2021 [8] |
| OPA 1.0 release | December 2025 [28] |
| Latest release | v1.14.0, February 26, 2026 [28] |

At graduation, OPA had 90+ contributors from ~30 organizations, with
maintainers from Google, Microsoft, VMware, and Styra [8]. Two external security
audits by Cure53 were completed during incubation [8]. The project achieved CII
Best Practices Badge certification [8].

**GitHub metrics** (as of research date): 11.5k stars, 1.5k forks [28].

**Notable adopters**: Goldman Sachs, Netflix, Pinterest, T-Mobile, Atlassian [8],
Intuit (50 clusters, 1,000 namespaces), Zalando (3,000 apps, 2,000 engineers),
Miro (in-process, <10ms requirement) [38].

## Ecosystem

- **Gatekeeper**: Kubernetes admission controller using OPA, 4.1k stars [28]
- **Conftest**: Configuration testing with Rego (Kubernetes, Terraform, Serverless) [39]
- **Regal**: Official OPA linter with 6 rule categories, language server integration [40]
- **OPAL**: Open Policy Administration Layer for real-time updates, built on FastAPI [14]
